Name: Deconvolve
Description: Regression-based, overlap-corrected ERPs (rERP) via the Unfold toolbox (Ehinger & Dimigen 2019; Dimigen & Ehinger 2021): an alternative to epoch-and-average that fits every bin at once against the whole continuous recording, so where events follow each other faster than a response decays each bin keeps its own response instead of a smear of its neighbours. Events in no bin are fitted as nuisance and dropped, and bad stretches are ignored in the model rather than removed as epochs. The result is shaped exactly like Average: one waveform per bin, read unchanged by Measure, ScalpDistribution, GrandAverage and the reports. Or, if asked, one overlap-corrected trial per event instead, shaped like a DefineBins epoch node: each event's recording with every other event's fitted response subtracted, for an ERP image without the overlap and for the data-quality report's trial measures (Average of them gives the waveforms back). Runs on the continuous recording and asks for the bins it should fit, in DefineBins' language, so it needs no epoched or pre-binned dataset (and cannot use one: epoching destroys the overlap it separates)
